gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Noto Sans Marchen reads big, its small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Edo SZ draws every stroke at one constant width, a flat, unmodulated line that gives the open curves below it something firm to lean on.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mayan-num: Noto Sans Mayan Numerals reads with lofty little letters and a c that gapes at any size. Paragraphs of it move briskly, while Edo SZ stays smooth as drawn wire.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-medefaidr: Edo SZ holds its stroke widths steady from stem to curve, a display face with a uniform line. Noto Sans Medefaidrin rises high in the lowercase and never pools ink where curves turn, so paragraphs read crisp.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mende-kik: Daylight shows through every curve here, and the lowercase stands proud against its capitals. Noto Sans Mende Kikakui keeps that up across a full paragraph, while Edo SZ above keeps rounds and stems uniform.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mono: Noto Sans Mono spaces its letters so generously that nothing bumps, and every curve opens wide. And Edo SZ does presence best, with strokes that never vary in width, where the body's strength is sturdy, large-looking words.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mro: Words in Noto Sans Mro look dense through the middle, and wide entrances lead into each letter. And Edo SZ brings the standout trait, strokes like twine pressed into a flat surface.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Edo SZ draws curves that never thin out at the turns, giving its display lowercase a cultural, classic weight. Noto Sans Nabataean reads openly, lowercase near cap height, s curves wide.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: A single constant stroke width, drawn like a marker tip, gives Edo SZ its cultural, classic look. But Noto Sans Nag Mundari does the quieter work, with half-unwrapped curves and lowercase that rivals the capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu reads large and light, with terminals held far from the stroke body and a towering x-height. And Edo SZ supplies the anchor: round bowls with walls of unvarying thickness.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Clean, cut-from-wire strokes give Edo SZ a display voice with a cultural, classic streak. Noto Sans Ogham looks bold because its lowercase bodies run so high, with wide gaps in the e.
